Quality and cost verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors

Tasks: 120 WideSWE tasks, one shared prompt each, historical ecosystem workspace. Configurations: seven (above); same scaffold for six (Claude Code), same model for two (GPT-5.6-sol on Codex CLI vs Claude Code). Baseline: none; RQ3 joint vs independent on 89 tasks with identical prompts, matched per-run limits (not total budget). Held constant: prompt, harness-level permissions, timeout policy, per-run resource limits; reasoning effort differs (high vs xhigh). Acceptance: hidden F2P and P2P tests, revised by rules reviewed by two authors and checked to reject base code and accept reference. Repetitions: one run per task and configuration (not stated as more). Human intervention: none

Codex CLI + GPT-5.6-sol best overall (42.50%), Claude Code + Qwen 3.8 Max best on bug fixes (48.33%), Gemini lowest (10.83%). Same model, Codex CLI vs Claude Code: 42.50% vs 32.50%, API 86.7 vs 134.8. All configurations lower on three-repository tasks. Joint vs independent: 40.45% vs 35.96% (20 of 89 tasks reverse); independent better on bug fixes (44.83 vs 34.48) and worse on features (31.67 vs 43.33) with 3.13x API requests. No significance tests; the authors call the recovery-rate difference (60.00% vs 9.43%) descriptive, not causal, and say the opposite net directions by task type should not be generalised beyond the sample
fields.why: The draft said the authors call 'the differences' descriptive; the text (App. B.1, p. 20) says this only of the recovery-rate difference, and separately warns against generalising the task-type reversal

fields.v: Distinguished configurations (10.83%-42.50%) and failure modes; single run per configuration, so repeatability not shown. Limitations stated: RQ3 matches per-run, not total budget; recovery difference descriptive, not causal; opposite net directions by task type not to be generalised
Tasks involve only two or three target repositories and Linux environments; results do not establish performance on more repositories or other platforms (Appendix D). No threats-to-validity section
